i.norm: Verifies that removeAll delegates removal to the underlying collection, so elements are removed from the backing list as well as the index. The null-key transformer maps every element to the same null key, meaning the indexed collection treats all elements as equivalent under the index. An element is added directly to the backing list (bypassing the indexed collection), then removeAll is called with that same list. Because removeAll iterates over the argument collection and calls remove() on the indexed collection (which in turn removes from the backing list), the element ends up removed from the backing list itself, leaving it empty.
Set up an empty backing list and a transformer that always produces a null key
Wrap the backing list in a non-unique indexed collection
Add an element directly to the backing list, bypassing the indexed collection
Remove all elements in backingList from the indexed collection; since the indexed collection's remove() delegates to the backing list, this also empties backingList
The backing list should now be empty because the element was removed through the index
removeAll should report that the collection changed
